1. ((S ∨ P) ↔ (S ↔ P))
2. (R ↔ Q)

**Analyzing Premise 1:**

Let me build a truth table for (S ∨ P) ↔ (S ↔ P):

| S | P | S∨P | S↔P | (S∨P)↔(S↔P) |
|---|---|------|-----|-------------|
| T | T |  T  |  T  |     T       |
| T | F |  T  |  F  |     F       |
| F | T |  T  |  F  |     F       |
| F | F |  F  |  T  |     F       |

The expression (S ∨ P) ↔ (S ↔ P) is true **only** when both S and P are true, which is exactly the truth table for S ∧ P.

Therefore: ((S ∨ P) ↔ (S ↔ P)) ≡ S ∧ P

Premise 2 (R ↔ Q) is simply a biconditional that doesn't combine with the other premise to produce a further simplification.

The key derivable conclusion is **S ∧ P**.

<answer>S ∧ P</answer>
